title: The classical fabric of a RISC-Q system
summary: How long a measured bit takes to reach another core, how fast boards synchronize, and how many bits per microsecond a board and a lane between boards carry. Every system call that moves a classical bit pays these costs.
method: Small firmware programs run on one to eight ZCU216-class boards at RISC-Q's 500 MHz clock: one core publishes a bit, every core meets at a barrier, cores publish bits back to back. Times come from the trace of each run.

A board's hub joins its cores. Between boards, RISC-Q's lane carries one 72-bit frame per published bit. With three or more boards, board 0 forwards between lanes, an extension of RISC-Q's two-board design. The lane's word-clock phase is arbitrary at power-up, so every lane-dependent probe is swept over all eight phases; the spread is a few cycles.

sections.heading: Cable delay between boards
sections.text: The lane delay L (transceiver and cable, in 16 ns word clocks) is not part of RISC-Q's RTL; its simulation uses 3. Both costs grow exactly linearly: a publish takes 324 + 8L cycles to another board, a barrier whose last arrival is remote 784 + 16L.

findings: A machine-wide classical bandwidth is two numbers 160 times apart: 500 bits/µs inside a board, 3.1 bits/µs across a lane. Syndrome bits have to stay on the board that measures them, or travel packed into words.
Publishing has no back-pressure: a burst larger than the hub's 8-deep queues loses bits. Firmware must pace its publishes, so the pacing belongs to the cost of a measurement.

Classical traffic delays synchronization: a bit published just before a barrier's release frame occupies the lane and delays the release on the far board by a frame (found in a Besedin et al. reproduction on two boards).
note: All numbers are measured on QuantumOS's Lean model of RISC-Q control hardware (its cores, hubs and lanes are checked against RISC-Q's RTL cycle for cycle), on generated or published hardware designs. They are properties of that model, not of laboratory hardware.
